clue.text: Tolerably recompensed men domiciled abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests being all over the place, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fairly paid workers who have settled in a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning a middling wage means being paid tolerably, neither rich nor poor.

clue.text: Holiday destination for a chick wearing hand-warmer? Not quite

indicators.note: the muff is worn around the other pieces, so it goes outside them
not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a muff is a fur tube for keeping the hands warm
chick is slang for a girl, a gal

explanation.surface: A young woman with a muff off on holiday somewhere sunny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims MUFF to MUF, which then holds A GAL. MAGALUF is a package-holiday resort on Majorca, famous with young British tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: Magaluf is a Spanish seaside resort, a popular place to go on holiday.

clue.text: Rising, also, to introduce Eastern instrument with strings — and guts!

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom up
AND takes in the next piece, putting it inside itself

parts.note: also means and
an oud is a lute-like stringed instrument of the Middle East

explanation.surface: An exotic stringed instrument is brought in, along with some gut strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' puts E inside, making ANED; 'Rising' turns the full run ANEDOUD upside down, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodena are the first sections of the small intestine, so they are part of the guts.

clue.text: Deposit tale about spirit

indicators.note: the fib goes around the drink, holding it inside

parts.note: a tale can be a fib or lie
mescal is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave

explanation.surface: A story about a ghost that leaves something behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Limescale is the chalky deposit hard water leaves in kettles and pipes.

clue.text: Draw conclusion that's right about far right, formerly

indicators.note: the first pieces go around the party, holding it inside

parts.note: that's, as in 'that is', is i.e. (id est)
the National Front, NF, was a British far-right party, prominent in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Concluding that something is correct about past right-wing extremism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' as i.e. is a standard abbreviation; the National Front still exists but its heyday is past, hence 'formerly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce, reaching a judgement from the evidence given.

clue.text: Hanger-on's about to hang on

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
to linger is to hang on or stay around

explanation.surface: A sponger is about to stay on.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinger is someone who sticks to others, a hanger-on or limpet.

clue.text: Spotted Mum adjusting a curl

parts.note: Ma is an informal name for mother

indicators.note: adjusting suggests rearranging, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum caught fixing a curl in her hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Macular means marked with spots, from macula, a spot or blotch.

clue.text: Murdered fence — by Spooner's account, a simple matter

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening sounds trade places

parts.note: murdered means slain
a paling is a fence made of pointed stakes

explanation.surface: A killing at a fence turns out to be straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of SLAIN PALING gives a phrase that sounds like the answer, with the spelling changed to SAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain sailing is an idiom for something easy and free of difficulty.

clue.text: Space in vehicle for the French man of the match?

parts.note: le is French for the
at a wedding, or match, the bridegroom is a key man

explanation.surface: The best player gets room in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the match' suggests sport, but the match is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the space for the legs in front of a seat in a car or plane.

clue.text: Justifiable apprehension of dandy taking possession of car I wrecked

indicators.note: the dandy holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a fop is a vain dandy

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dandy is rightly arrested for stealing a car he then crashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' makes AIRC from the clue's car I; 'apprehension' means arrest, not anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair cop is a fair arrest, the idiom used by a criminal admitting being caught.

clue.text: 26s about to reference proboscis-owner with elephant's head in footnote

indicators.note: the reversed pieces sit inside the footnote

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

indicators.note: about means turned around, so these pieces are written backwards

parts.note: to cite is to reference
the tapir has a short trunk, or proboscis

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Aristotle's followers cite an animal with a trunk in a footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the run into ERIPATETIC. 26s means the answer to 26 Across, Aristotelians, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peripatetics were Aristotle's school, named for walking about while teaching.

clue.text: Second one individually removed from buffoonery in disorder

indicators.note: each named letter is taken out of the word on its own

parts.note: buffoonery is silliness, foolish behaviour
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Clowning around causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S and one I from SILLINESS; the I taken is the second one.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorder is a sickness or ailment of body or mind.

clue.text: Familiar face (not constipated)

definitions.meaning: a frequent customer, someone always seen in a pub or shop
having bowel movements as normal and on schedule

explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a habitual customer; being regular also means having normal bowel movements.

clue.text: Capital I in "item of furniture"

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the furniture

parts.note: a sofa is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A letter I written inside a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Female rep actor reaped second harvest

indicators.note: reaped crops are cut and gathered up, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman in repertory theatre brings in a second harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftercrop is a further crop taken from the same land in one season.

clue.text: Turn on poorly-fed bird first

indicators.note: the bird comes first, before the other piece

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
ill ate means fed poorly

explanation.surface: A hungry bird is the first to arouse interest.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse, to get someone going.

clue.text: Undiplomatic about monarch's rash

indicators.note: the cheeky word goes around the monarch

parts.note: impudent means cheeky, lacking tact
R, for rex or regina, stands for a monarch

explanation.surface: A tactless remark about the king is reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means unwise and heedless, which is to say rash.

clue.text: Extreme uprising internally democratic

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: polar means at the extreme, the opposite pole
the word up, rising in a down clue, is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: An extreme revolt within is democratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' inside the one word 'uprising' turns UP over, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular means of or by the people, the sense of democratic.

clue.text: Lousy tennis player previously entering America

indicators.note: the player goes into the country

parts.note: US is America
Monica Seles was a top tennis player of the 1990s

explanation.surface: A bad former tennis star moves to America.
explanation.definitionFit: Lousy and useless are both slang for bad or no good.

clue.text: Trainee rebel given time

parts.note: Jack Cade led a revolt in England in 1450

explanation.surface: A trainee rebel is given time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the armed forces or the police.

clue.text: Apparently gay terrorists once raised drink

parts.note: camp means flamboyant or effeminate in manner

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written from the bottom up

parts.note: the IRA, Irish Republican Army, was once a terrorist group

explanation.surface: A flamboyant ex-terrorist knocks back a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is a bitter Italian aperitif, a drink.

clue.text: Bearer of barrels of fragrant oil covering girl up

the oil covers the girl, so she goes inside it

Amy is a girl's name

clue.text: Win admiration of conscript

definitions.meaning: to earn the respect of someone
to force into military service, as a press gang did

explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to awe someone, and also to force men into the navy.

clue.text: Authorisation expresses nothing

parts.note: says means expresses
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A permit says nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their permission or authority to do something.

clue.text: Slate educated business person in terminal

parts.note: terminal means last
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

parts.note: all means everything

clue.text: … a cinema having turned pale

indicators.note: having turned around, these letters are rearranged
